replies.author: Demintika
replies.body:
That's what I noticed from a recently released game I wish-listed. It used AI a lot for assets.

Most of the reviews are non-English (mostly from Asia and Russia), showing a Mostly Positive (\~70%). Not sure what they say though.

But, 90% of English reviews are Negative. Individually, those reviews sound pretty fair for someone who hasn't played the game and was just looking at review, pointing out various flaws of the game, and the "downside" of AI usage is just a footnote in those reviews.

comments.author: EmperorsShadow
comments.body: The effort spent on it matters a lot more than if its Ai or not. They definitely polished it. There is like 8+ hours of footage in it that made the cut, so the actual process likely took months if not years. The story is quite solid. 30 voice actors, and video editors who understand cinematography to sort though hundreds of hours of generated footage not to mention  the storyboarding and the lora+storyboarding+sketching to generate the right footage. On top of that the amount of compute used is likely not cheap. So its a team of funded professionals who spent months on it.

replies.author: Live_Fall3452
replies.body: Yeah, this puts the lie to the argument that there’s no skill or learning curve to AI art. There’s very obviously a huge learning curve from amateurs to professionals, and that learning curve is likely to get longer over time as people advance new ways of pulling the most they can out of the technology.
